verdicts.why: Describes the word's force under 'disregarded' (attention owed and not paid) against its neighbour *ignored*, stays inside the word, negative charge fits, and the Shaw example is this sense.
Places the word within the synset by force alone (something stood there to be attended to, without deliberateness or failure of care), matches 'disregarded', and the example fits.
A miss rather than a refusal that concedes the thing should have counted is exactly 'not taken into account' with a mild negative charge, and nothing leaves the word.
Contrasts with *overlooked* on force only (flat, conceding no mistake), agrees with the gloss, neutral charge is plausible, and the retirement example is this sense.
The plain negative of taking into account with no implied obligation matches the gloss and the neutral charge, and the note stays inside the word.
The implied watcher who might have noticed, making it relief or slight, is a description of the word's force under 'unnoticed', and neutral charge fits that two-way reading.
Distinguishes it from *unobserved* by what the word itself implies (no watcher), agrees with 'unnoticed', neutral charge fits, and 'unseen forces at work' is this sense.
Covers both halves of the gloss with the weight on perceiving, 'formal' is a permitted register label, and the neutral charge is plausible.
Tips the same gloss pair toward the not-commented-on half without narrowing past the gloss's 'or', stays inside the word, and neutral charge fits.
Restates both limbs of the gloss (nothing fresh in it, nothing fresh from it) and sets the force against *trite*; negative charge and both examples fit.
Dismissal that the repetition has emptied the thing out is the gloss's overuse read as force, contrasted with *commonplace* on force alone, negative charge fits.

Claims to be 'the mildest reproach in the set', but the sibling notes for *stock* ('flattest word here, almost a category rather than a fault') and *timeworn* ('softer than the rest') each claim the same bottom rung, so at most one of these superlatives can hold and stock's is the better founded.
A verdict that the thing has been run into the ground, weighed against *tired*, matches the gloss; 'formal-sounding' is register, and the example fits.
Informal is a register label, the shrug at overfamiliarity versus *banal*'s condemnation is a force contrast within the gloss, and negative charge is still plausible.
The handled-until-the-shine-came-off image is the word's own metaphor read as force, contrasted with *well-worn*, and it stays on overuse as glossed.

Filing the repetition almost as a category rather than a fault is a defensible account of this word's near-absence of reproach, the 'almost' keeps the negative charge plausible, and 'a stock answer' fits.
Wear gone all the way through with nothing left inside is the gloss's overuse rendered through the word's own image, contrasted with *well-worn*; example fits.

'Softer than the rest' is a synset-wide superlative that collides with *commonplace* ('mildest reproach in the set') and *stock* ('flattest word here'); the reasoning about wear laid at time's door is sound, but the superlative cannot be true alongside those two notes.
